title: Norse Mythology
text: Norse mythology is the body of myths of the North Germanic peoples, comprising Old Norse religion and pre-Christian Scandinavian mythology. The Norse pantheon is headed by Odin, the Allfather, and includes Thor (god of thunder), Loki (a trickster), Freya (goddess of love and war), and Baldur (god of light). The Norse cosmology features nine interconnected worlds, including Asgard (home of the gods), Midgard (Earth), and Hel (the underworld), connected by the world tree Yggdrasil. Norse mythology predicts a cataclysmic final battle called Ragnarök, in which many gods will die. The myths were primarily recorded in Icelandic texts such as the Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda compiled by Snorri Sturluson in the 13th century.
